name: Question 12
worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{x+1}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=27(x+1)^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 27(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x=9(x+1)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27(x+1)^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}(9(x+1)^{3})-\int (9(x+1)^{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =9(x+1)^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-18\int (x+1)^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int (x+1)^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1) & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x+1}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=(x+1)^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int (x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+1)^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)(\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int (x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{3}-\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27(x+1)^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2}\,\text{d}x & =9(x+1)^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-18\int (x+1)^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =9(x+1)^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-18(\frac{(x+1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)}{3}-\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{9}+D) \\  & =9(x+1)^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-6(x+1)^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+2(x+1)^{3}-18D \\  & =(x+1)^{3}(9{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-18D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{e-1}27(x+1)^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))^{2}\text{d}x & ={[(x+1)^{3}(9{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1))}^{2}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+2)]}_{0}^{e-1} \\  & =[{e}^{3}(9{(\operatorname{ln}⁡e)}^{2}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡e+2)]-[{1}^{3}(9{(\operatorname{ln}⁡1)}^{2}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2)] \\  & =[{e}^{3}(9-6+2)]-2 \\  & =5{e}^{3}-2\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=(ln⁡(x+1))2⟹dudx=2ln⁡(x+1)x+1,dvdx=27(x+1)2⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫27(x+1)2dx=9(x+1)3.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫27(x+1)2(ln⁡(x+1))2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(ln⁡(x+1))2(9(x+1)3)−∫(9(x+1)3)(2ln⁡(x+1)x+1)dx=9(x+1)3(ln⁡(x+1))2−18∫(x+1)2ln⁡(x+1)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫(x+1)2ln⁡(x+1)dx. We take u=ln⁡(x+1)⟹dudx=1x+1,dvdx=(x+1)2⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫(x+1)2dx=(x+1)33.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫(x+1)2ln⁡(x+1)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=ln⁡(x+1)((x+1)33)−∫((x+1)33)(1x+1)dx=(x+1)3ln⁡(x+1)3−13∫(x+1)2dx=(x+1)3ln⁡(x+1)3−(x+1)39+D, where D is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫27(x+1)2(ln⁡(x+1))2dx=9(x+1)3(ln⁡(x+1))2−18∫(x+1)2ln⁡(x+1)dx=9(x+1)3(ln⁡(x+1))2−18((x+1)3ln⁡(x+1)3−(x+1)39+D)=9(x+1)3(ln⁡(x+1))2−6(x+1)3ln⁡(x+1)+2(x+1)3−18D=(x+1)3(9(ln⁡(x+1))2−6ln⁡(x+1)+2)+C, where C=−18D.

Finally, we can work out the definite integral: ∫0e−127(x+1)2(ln⁡(x+1))2dx=[(x+1)3(9(ln⁡(x+1))2−6ln⁡(x+1)+2)]0e−1=[e3(9(ln⁡e)2−6ln⁡e+2)]−[13(9(ln⁡1)2−6ln⁡1+2)]=[e3(9−6+2)]−2=5e3−2
